result_snapshot.likely_cost: Without a repair move, clear expression may land as rigid or closed.
result_snapshot.minimal_action: After tension, try: “The way I said that may have landed badly. I want to add what I meant.”
result_snapshot.share_safe_sentence: This result reminds me: after clarity, repair can still be added.
result_snapshot.continue_path: Save the report; to observe change, retest after 30–90 days or after a meaningful life change.

scientific_contract.test_definition: This report comes from your self-descriptions across 60 items. It organizes emotional awareness, regulation, empathic understanding, and relational-action tendencies in this response session; it is not external observation or an objective ability test.
scientific_contract.self_report_statement: EQ-60 is a self-report tool. The result can support reflection, tracking, and review, but it cannot directly prove how you perform in real situations.
scientific_contract.non_clinical_statement: This report is not for clinical diagnosis, treatment evaluation, medical advice, crisis decisions, or psychological risk assessment. If distress keeps affecting sleep, work, interpersonal safety, or daily functioning, seek qualified professional or real-world support.
scientific_contract.non_hiring_statement: This result must not be used for hiring, selection, rejection, promotion, role assignment, performance review, team screening, or any high-stakes organizational decision. It should not be used to judge whether another person is suitable for a role.
scientific_contract.non_ability_statement: EQ-60 is not an emotional-ability test, MSCEIT, certification, clinical tool, or hiring tool. It cannot prove communication, relationship, or work ability.
scientific_contract.norm_status_statement: Read standard scores, percentiles, and bands with the reference version stated in the report. With a bootstrap or other model-based reference, percentiles are estimated from model parameters, not observed sample ranks. With sample-based norms, use the stated reference group and version. They do not rank ability, worth, or career competitiveness.
scientific_contract.quality_rules_statement: Interpretation confidence considers response speed, repeated identical choices, extreme choices, neutral choices, and consistency signals. Low-confidence results should be treated primarily as response-quality guidance and retest advice, not as strong profiling, career conclusions, or practice recommendations.
scientific_contract.version_statement: The report records item, scoring, norm, and content versions for retest comparison and quality tracking; version numbers do not confer clinical, hiring, or ability certification.
scientific_contract.user_safe_summary: Use it for self-understanding, relational reflection, low-risk communication practice, and work-environment variable review.
scientific_contract.do_not_overread: Read the report as an interpretive sketch of this self-report session, not for clinical diagnosis, hiring, career prediction, job-performance prediction, or evaluation of another person.

global_index.label: Emotional & Relational Functioning Index
global_index.definition: The index combines four self-report dimensions into a reading entry for the emotional and relational self-perception pattern shown in this response session.
global_index.not_a_capability_score: It is not an emotional-ability score, live-performance score, career-competitiveness score, or final global norm ranking; use it as navigation into dimensions and scene explanations.
global_index.how_to_use: Use the overview first, then return to dimensions, response quality, evidence status, and real-life scenes. Do not use the total score by itself to judge yourself or others.

score_notes.percentile: A percentile depends on the reference version stated in the report: a bootstrap or other model-based reference gives a position estimated from model parameters, not an observed sample rank; sample-based norms should be read with the stated reference group and version. It is not an ability ranking, true-level ranking, final global norm, or career-competitiveness ranking.
score_notes.standard_score: Standard score supports stable display and dimension comparison. It is a reading entry, not proof of live performance or ability.
score_notes.band: Bands reduce reading effort; they are not fixed identities, credentials, clinical findings, hiring signals, or career judgments.
score_notes.provisional_norm: Current norms are provisional. Future samples, language versions, and content versions may change interpretation boundaries.
score_notes.commercial_boundary: The total score should not be used alone; full interpretation requires dimensions, quality, evidence status, mechanisms, and scene boundaries.

foundational.label: Foundational
foundational.meaning: The current self-report signal suggests starting with clearer recognition, naming, and reset habits.
foundational.strength: Small repeatable actions can create more stable progress.
foundational.risk: Jumping into complex communication tactics may frustrate you if the base signal is unclear.
foundational.practice_focus: Name one emotion daily and pair it with one low-cost reset action.
foundational.do_not_overread: Use this band as a practice starting point, not an ability floor.

developing.label: Developing
developing.meaning: You have a usable base, but consistency may drop during feedback, pressure, or relational tension.
developing.strength: You already catch part of the signal and can turn it into a routine.
developing.risk: The common trap is knowing something but not using it in the moment.
developing.practice_focus: Pick one frequent scene and prepare one response sentence.
developing.do_not_overread: It describes this session’s self-rating, not how you always act.

stable.label: Stable
stable.meaning: In many everyday settings, these emotional and relational patterns are easier to use, with specific triggers still visible.
stable.strength: Your result can support more precise scene-based practice.
stable.risk: Stability does not mean no cost, especially in high-intensity relational environments.
stable.practice_focus: Identify one scene where stability drops and review it afterward.
stable.do_not_overread: “Stable” can change with pressure and context; it is not trait proof.

proficient.label: Proficient
proficient.meaning: You can usually recognize, regulate, and handle relational signals with good consistency.
proficient.strength: You can turn personal strengths into repeatable communication habits.
proficient.risk: Others may assume you should always be the stabilizing person.
proficient.practice_focus: Move from “I can handle this” to “I choose how to handle this.”
proficient.do_not_overread: “Proficient” is not an ability credential or a duty to stabilize others.

integrated.label: Integrated
integrated.meaning: The four signals often work together, helping you hold self, others, and the relationship goal in view.
integrated.strength: You can systematize strengths into boundaries, repair, and recovery rhythm.
integrated.risk: High integration may still create over-responsibility and high-standard fatigue.
integrated.practice_focus: Build recovery boundaries so stabilizing others does not become your default duty.
integrated.do_not_overread: “Integrated” does not mean no blind spots and is not for career decisions.

SA.label: Self-Awareness
SA.definition: A self-reported tendency to notice emotions, triggers, body signals, and current needs; it is not externally observed self-knowledge ability and does not guarantee clear expression in the moment.
SA.what_high_can_look_like: You can often identify feelings and triggers quickly, while still needing to turn awareness into action.
SA.what_low_can_look_like: Feelings may become clear only afterward, making it easier to react before understanding.
SA.development_question: What am I actually feeling and needing right now?
SA.do_not_overread: The Self-Awareness score describes a relative tendency in this self-report session; it is not proof of ability, a fixed label, a diagnosis, or a prediction of external behavior.

ER.label: Emotion Regulation
ER.definition: A self-reported tendency to pause, reset, and choose responses after pressure, feedback, frustration, or conflict; it is not the same as always staying calm, suppressing emotion, or proving resilience.
ER.what_high_can_look_like: You can often pause, recover, and choose a response under pressure, without being emotionless.
ER.what_low_can_look_like: Recovery may take longer after being triggered, with avoidance, over-explaining, or suppression becoming common.
ER.development_question: Can I lower the heat first before choosing my response?
ER.do_not_overread: The Emotion Regulation score describes a relative tendency in this self-report session; it is not proof of ability, a fixed label, a diagnosis, or a prediction of external behavior.

EM.label: Empathy
EM.definition: A self-reported tendency to understand others’ emotional cues, perspectives, and possible feelings; it may reflect cognitive and affective empathy signals, but it is not mind-reading accuracy, prosocial behavior, or taking on others’ distress.
EM.what_high_can_look_like: You can notice others’ emotional states, while still needing boundaries against over-absorbing.
EM.what_low_can_look_like: You may focus on tasks or facts and miss some emotional cues.
EM.development_question: What is the other person really concerned about?
EM.do_not_overread: The Empathy score describes a relative tendency in this self-report session; it is not proof of ability, a fixed label, a diagnosis, or a prediction of external behavior.

RM.label: Relationship Management
RM.definition: A self-reported tendency around expression, collaboration, boundaries, and relationship repair; it does not directly predict relationship quality, leadership, popularity, or others’ evaluations.
RM.what_high_can_look_like: You can maintain communication and relationship quality, while still watching for honest expression and boundaries.
RM.what_low_can_look_like: Even when feelings are clear, repairing or moving the conversation forward may be harder.
RM.development_question: How can I say this honestly while keeping the conversation open?
RM.do_not_overread: The Relationship Management score describes a relative tendency in this self-report session; it is not proof of ability, a fixed label, a diagnosis, or a prediction of external behavior.

core_formulation.title: Self-reported pattern: Clear self-position, weaker repair moves
core_formulation.one_liner: In this self-report, you seem relatively clear about your feelings and position, while post-conflict repair, reopening dialogue, or lowering defensiveness may be less consistent.
core_formulation.core_claim: This does not mean you “cannot handle relationships.” It separates clear expression from relational repair as two different steps.
evidence_basis: The four relative dimension positions and response quality support this interpretation; check it against real situations.
core_formulation.primary_strength: You may be able to state why something bothers you, where you disagree, or what you need.
core_formulation.likely_cost: Without repair, clear expression can be experienced by others as final, rejecting, or distant.
core_formulation.development_lever: Add a repair sentence after expression: I want to be clear about the issue and still keep the relationship open for dialogue.
core_formulation.do_not_overread: Check this interpretation against real feedback and specific situations; it does not replace behavioral observation.
core_formulation.share_line: This self-report suggests you may know your position clearly, while repair after tension can become more concrete.

mechanisms.title: Emotion regulation x relationship management: chain still forming
mechanisms.why_it_matters: This mechanism focuses on how regulation under pressure connects to communication, repair, and boundaries. It helps locate which link in the chain needs observation, but it cannot by itself predict real-world behavior.
mechanisms.what_it_feels_like: When both sides feel less available in self-report, this mechanism is better treated as a practice entry point than as a conclusion.
mechanisms.strength: The useful part is that the issue becomes smaller and can be practiced in a low-risk situation.
mechanisms.cost: The cost is that labeling too quickly can turn trainable steps into a fixed-deficit story.
mechanisms.development_lever: Next practice focus: Under pressure, slow the response first, then choose repair, boundary, or pause. Use it as a concrete review entry point, not proof of a fixed deficit.
mechanisms.micro_action: Micro-action: in the next similar scene, add only one step. Under pressure, slow the response first, then choose repair, boundary, or pause.
mechanisms.do_not_overread: Check settling pressure before taking relational action in a real situation; the ER_RM score combination does not establish cause or ability.

mechanisms.title: Self-awareness x emotion regulation: coordinated strengths
mechanisms.why_it_matters: This mechanism focuses on how noticing your inner state connects to recovery and response. It helps locate which link in the chain needs observation, but it cannot by itself predict real-world behavior.
mechanisms.what_it_feels_like: In this self-report, both parts of noticing your inner state and making room to recover feel available; stress and relationship safety may still change what happens.
mechanisms.strength: The useful possibility is a clearer link in noticing your inner state and making room to recover.
mechanisms.cost: The risk is treating this smooth self-rating as stable ability and missing context around noticing your inner state and making room to recover.
mechanisms.development_lever: Next practice focus: After naming the emotion, add one slowing or recovery step. Use it as a concrete review entry point, not proof of a fixed deficit.
mechanisms.micro_action: Micro-action: in the next similar scene, add only one step. After naming the emotion, add one slowing or recovery step.
mechanisms.do_not_overread: Check noticing your inner state and making room to recover in a real situation; the SA_ER score combination does not establish cause or ability.

reality_scenes.title: Team collaboration: translate atmosphere into roles
reality_scenes.typical_response: This response suggests the self-perceived pattern “Clear self-position, weaker repair moves.” In teamwork, check whether you quietly take on emotional coordination or gap-filling beyond the task itself.
reality_scenes.strength: The useful possibility is noticing task and relationship demands together, then making hidden work explicit.
reality_scenes.cost: When roles are unclear, the person most willing to coordinate can inherit unnamed responsibility.
reality_scenes.better_move: Do one thing: rewrite the current difficulty as roles, one owner, and a deadline.
reality_scenes.micro_script: Who owns this, when is it due, and who decides if it gets blocked?
reality_scenes.reflection_question: Are you completing your role, or carrying coordination work the team has not named?
reality_scenes.reflection_prompt: Record the owner, deadline, and who decides when work is blocked.
reality_scenes.do_not_overread: This is a teamwork observation, not a judgment of anyone's ability.
reality_scenes.why_this_matters: Converts team atmosphere into roles and process that can be checked.
reality_scenes.tiny_experiment: Before the next collaboration, record the owner, decision maker, and deadline.
reality_scenes.result_page_depth: For teamwork review, not for judging team or individual performance.
reality_scenes.context: When several people work with unclear goals, overlapping responsibility, or uneven pace.

reality_scenes.title: Pressure recovery: recover before committing
reality_scenes.typical_response: This response suggests the self-perceived pattern “Clear self-position, weaker repair moves.” As pressure accumulates, check whether you notice reduced attention instead of treating endurance as steadiness.
reality_scenes.strength: The useful possibility is treating fatigue as a state that needs care, not as a character flaw.
reality_scenes.cost: Without recovery, regulation can become suppression and later appear as numbness, escalation, or avoidance.
reality_scenes.better_move: Do one thing: schedule a defined short pause before explaining, committing, or deciding.
reality_scenes.micro_script: I need ten minutes to recover my attention, then I can give you a clear response.
reality_scenes.reflection_question: Can you still understand the information and decide, or are you only sustaining a reaction?
reality_scenes.reflection_prompt: Record the pressure cue, pause length, and response after recovery.
reality_scenes.do_not_overread: Persistent sleep loss, severe distress, or impaired functioning needs real-world support, not only a micro-practice.
reality_scenes.why_this_matters: Turns endurance into one explicit, schedulable recovery step.
reality_scenes.tiny_experiment: At the next pressure spike, take one short pause and then note whether the decision became clearer.
reality_scenes.result_page_depth: For recovery-rhythm review, not for clinical or functioning judgments.
reality_scenes.context: After sustained demand, urgency, or emotional load, when communication or a decision is still required.

reality_scenes.title: Work-environment conditions to verify
reality_scenes.typical_response: This response suggests the self-perceived pattern “Clear self-position, weaker repair moves.” It cannot decide which role fits; it only points to work conditions worth checking for communication load, boundaries, and recovery.
reality_scenes.strength: The useful possibility is turning an abstract result into questions for a real team or role.
reality_scenes.cost: Treating environment preferences as job fit can miss actual duties, culture, management, and life stage.
reality_scenes.better_move: Do one thing: verify whether people can pause, ask for help, or hand off work as pressure rises.
reality_scenes.micro_script: When pressure rises here, can people pause, ask for help, or hand work off?
reality_scenes.reflection_question: Is feedback specific, can conflict pause, are boundaries respected, and can recovery be planned?
reality_scenes.reflection_prompt: Record one real environment, observable evidence, and one open question.
reality_scenes.do_not_overread: These are conditions to verify, not evidence of job fit, selection, or performance.
reality_scenes.why_this_matters: Replaces a career judgment with a check of actual work conditions.
reality_scenes.tiny_experiment: Choose one real team and answer this environment question from public rules or direct experience.
reality_scenes.result_page_depth: For checking work conditions, not for job-fit or performance prediction.
reality_scenes.context: When checking team norms, management style, feedback rhythm, interpersonal density, and recovery space.

career_environment.label: Conflict frequency: medium
career_environment.meaning: how often disagreement, complaints, negotiation, trade-offs, or high-pressure conversations appear
career_environment.fit_signal: Observe whether disagreement has clear rules for pausing, escalation, and repair.
career_environment.strain_signal: Possible strain condition: if rules, power differences, support, and recovery space are unclear, medium conflict frequency can still create pressure.
career_environment.interview_question: When conflict appears, does the team use facts, roles, and process, or personal relationships?
role_observation_checklist: Whether disagreements are documented and reviewed
Whether power differences shape who can speak
Whether there is a safe exit or escalation path
career_environment.team_risk: Without conflict rules, buffering often falls to the person most willing to yield.
career_environment.recovery_condition: Check who can pause a conflict, who decides, and how collaboration resumes.
career_environment.what_to_verify: When conflict appears, does the team use facts, roles, and process, or personal relationships? Also observe the actual role, organization culture, management style, power structure, team resources, and your current life context.
career_environment.do_not_overread: Conflict frequency is not evidence that you can or cannot do a job.

career_environment.label: Feedback intensity: medium
career_environment.meaning: how often the work involves evaluation, revision, review, public comparison, or fast iteration
career_environment.fit_signal: Observe feedback frequency, specificity, and room to make corrections.
career_environment.strain_signal: Possible strain condition: if rules, power differences, support, and recovery space are unclear, medium feedback intensity can still create pressure.
career_environment.interview_question: Is feedback specific, regular, and able to separate task issues from personal judgment?
role_observation_checklist: Whether feedback targets behavior rather than character
Whether there is time and resource to revise
Whether comparison or humiliation is used
career_environment.team_risk: When feedback rules are vague, evaluation can turn into guesswork or emotional load.
career_environment.recovery_condition: Check whether feedback names behavior and allows clarification and review.
career_environment.what_to_verify: Is feedback specific, regular, and able to separate task issues from personal judgment? Also observe the actual role, organization culture, management style, power structure, team resources, and your current life context.
career_environment.do_not_overread: Feedback intensity cannot predict your performance or selection outcome.

action_prescription.title: Repair After Impact
action_prescription.why_this_matters: Move from “I did not mean it” to “I see the impact and I want to repair it.”
action_prescription.do_today: Today, use one low-risk version of this sentence: “What I said may have landed as dismissive. I want to try again, and first I want to hear how it landed for you.”
action_prescription.script: What I said may have landed as dismissive. I want to try again, and first I want to hear how it landed for you.

seven_day_plan.practice: Write the real impact of one tense moment.
Replace “I didn’t mean it” with “I see the impact.”
Practice one repair line after a small misunderstanding.
Ask what the other person heard.
Add one concrete corrective action.
Review whether repair made the relationship clearer.
Name the repair step you usually skip.

action_prescription.common_failure: The common failure is not lack of knowledge. It is remembering the tool only after the emotion is already high.
action_prescription.repair_move: If you miss it, do not restart the whole plan. Review one trigger and one first sentence for next time.
action_prescription.watch_out: Do not treat this practice as a demand to change yourself or another person immediately. Use it only in low-risk, exit-safe situations without clear coercion or power pressure, and look for one clearer pause, sentence, or review.
action_prescription.do_not_overread: Treat “Repair After Impact” as low-risk self-observation and communication preparation, not therapy, crisis support, a guarantee of relationship repair, or advice for unsafe, coercive, abusive, trauma-triggering, or clearly power-imbalanced situations. If safety, ongoing distress, or high-conflict dynamics are involved, prioritize trusted support or professional help.

sjt_bridge.title: Current report scope
sjt_bridge.description: This report contains the EQ-60 self-report result only; it contains no scenario-task result.
sjt_bridge.what_it_adds: There is currently no scenario-task data to interpret.
sjt_bridge.what_it_is_not: This is not MSCEIT and does not provide objective ability evidence.
sjt_bridge.do_not_overread: This page provides no scenario-task entry or conclusion.

boundary.title: Cross-Assessment Context Boundary
boundary.summary: This module only explains how related assessments can support reading the EQ-60 result. It does not combine multiple tests into a more “true” conclusion.
boundary.how_to_use: Treat MBTI, Big Five, Enneagram, RIASEC, and related results as reflection signals from different question frameworks. They can help form better questions, but they do not rewrite EQ scores, replace EQ-60 self-report, or prove real-world behavior.
boundary.claim_boundary: Not for emotional-ability ranking, career prediction, hiring, clinical diagnosis, relationship-outcome judgment, fixed identity labels, or high-stakes decisions.

quality_confidence.label: High interpretation confidence
quality_confidence.body: Your response pace and consistency support normal report reading.
quality_confidence.user_guidance: You can read the core pattern, dimension summary, and action suggestions while keeping them as self-report interpretation, not ability ranking or external evaluation.
quality_confidence.retest_note: If you want to observe change, retest after 30–90 days or after a meaningful life change.
quality_confidence.why_this_level: Speed, repeated choices, extreme/neutral responding, and consistency signals did not show a clear response-quality risk.
quality_confidence.how_to_read: Start with the key finding and supporting scores, then compare the selected scenes with your recent experience.
quality_confidence.what_to_trust: The relative dimension pattern, selected interpretation, and selected scenes can be read with normal confidence.
quality_confidence.what_to_hold_lightly: Specific scores, percentiles, and bands use a provisional reference. Model-based references are not observed sample ranks; sample-based references apply only to the stated group and version. Do not treat them as precise ability rankings, diagnoses, or career judgments.

psychometric_evidence_status.body: Current standard scores, percentiles, and bands use a provisional reference. A bootstrap or other model-based reference estimates position from model parameters, rather than observed sample ranks; sample-based norms should be read with the stated reference group and version. These are not final global norms, ability rankings, or real-world performance rankings.
psychometric_evidence_status.do_not_overread: Check the reference version first: a bootstrap or other model-based reference is not an observed sample rank, and sample-based norms apply only to the stated reference group and version.
psychometric_evidence_status.what_this_means_for_user: Scores can help locate this response pattern roughly against the stated reference, but should not be used to compare personal worth, ability level, career prospects, or relationship quality.
psychometric_evidence_status.next_validation_step: Continue expanding samples, stratify by language/region/age and related variables, and publish norm-version notes with interpretation limits.

psychometric_evidence_status.body: EQ-60 items, the four-dimension structure, and result-page interpretations have been mapped to self-reported emotional and relational functioning. The current evidence mainly supports content coverage and interpretation boundaries, not formal criterion validation or ability measurement.
psychometric_evidence_status.do_not_overread: Current evidence supports content coverage and interpretation boundaries only.
psychometric_evidence_status.what_this_means_for_user: Use the report as a structured self-reflection tool for organizing self-perceived signals in awareness, regulation, empathy, and relationship management.
psychometric_evidence_status.next_validation_step: Continue review by psychometric, boundary, and localization reviewers for item coverage, dimension assignment, cultural context, and misinterpretation risk.

psychometric_evidence_status.body: Internal consistency should be estimated by language, region, and dimension after sufficient sample accumulation, with version tracking for item and report changes. The current page should not imply completed reliability evidence.
psychometric_evidence_status.do_not_overread: Internal-consistency evidence still needs accumulation by language and dimension.
psychometric_evidence_status.what_this_means_for_user: Dimension scores can help read this response pattern, but should not be treated as fully reliability-validated stable measures.
psychometric_evidence_status.next_validation_step: After sample growth, report alpha/omega or more suitable reliability indices by dimension and inspect the effect of low-quality responses on estimates.

psychometric_evidence_status.body: The four-dimension model currently serves as the report interpretation framework. Suitable exploratory/confirmatory analyses are still needed to test whether items consistently support SA, ER, EM, and RM.
psychometric_evidence_status.do_not_overread: The four-dimension structure still needs testing in larger samples.
psychometric_evidence_status.what_this_means_for_user: The four-quadrant matrix is useful for organizing the report, but should not be read as a fully cross-sample-validated final factor model.
psychometric_evidence_status.next_validation_step: Use larger samples to examine EFA/CFA results, item loadings, dimension correlations, and model fit, with separate checks by language version.

psychometric_evidence_status.body: Test-retest stability still needs observation over appropriate time windows. EQ-60 is self-report, so recent stress, relationship events, and response state may influence results.
psychometric_evidence_status.do_not_overread: Compare trends after 30–90 days or a meaningful life change.
psychometric_evidence_status.what_this_means_for_user: If your recent circumstances have shifted substantially, read this result as a current self-report snapshot rather than a permanent label.
psychometric_evidence_status.next_validation_step: Compare retests over reasonable windows such as 30–90 days to separate stable self-perception, situational fluctuation, and low-quality response effects.

psychometric_evidence_status.body: Measurement invariance across Chinese/English versions, regions, and user groups still needs testing. Without invariance evidence, score meanings should not be directly compared across languages or groups.
psychometric_evidence_status.do_not_overread: Scores should not be directly compared across languages or groups.
psychometric_evidence_status.what_this_means_for_user: Both Chinese and English reports can support localized self-reflection, but percentile differences across languages, cultures, or groups should not be read as ability differences.
psychometric_evidence_status.next_validation_step: Check DIF, item interpretation differences, dimension structure, and score distributions by language and major user group; adjust interpretation where needed rather than forcing equivalence.

psychometric_evidence_status.body: External-association evidence is not being used to support high-stakes decisions. Future work may only explore links with low-risk indicators such as self-reported recovery, communication satisfaction, or growth-goal completion.
psychometric_evidence_status.do_not_overread: Current results cannot predict relationship, work, or health outcomes.
psychometric_evidence_status.what_this_means_for_user: The result does not prove job performance, relationship outcomes, mental-health status, or career success. It is a reference for self-understanding and low-risk action planning.
psychometric_evidence_status.next_validation_step: Design low-risk, non-hiring, non-clinical external-indicator studies and state clearly that association is not prediction or causation.

result_page_depth_modules.body: Start with one “this response pattern suggests” statement, check one evidence point, then choose one low-risk action. Do not treat the report as a personality verdict, ability ranking, or relationship diagnosis.

result_page_depth_modules.title: How to read the evidence
result_page_depth_modules.body: This report reads four self-report dimensions, dimension gaps, response quality, and the selected reading order together. It gives structure to interpretation; it does not reduce you to an ability score.
bullets: Dimension signals: self-reported SA / ER / EM / RM positions
Gap signal: strongest dimension and current next practice focus

Observation focus: which scenes and actions are worth checking first
result_page_depth_modules.what_this_does_not_mean: “How to read the evidence” only organizes this self-report session; it is not ability, diagnosis, hiring, or career-prediction evidence.

result_page_depth_modules.title: Reality check
result_page_depth_modules.body: For the next week, observe three low-risk signals: whose emotion you notice first, whether you can state one boundary, and roughly how long recovery takes afterward. In high-conflict, trauma-related, unsafe, or high-power-difference situations, do not use this report as a substitute for professional support.

result_page_depth_modules.title: Next observation path
result_page_depth_modules.body: This module turns “self-clear with weaker repair signals” into an observable, low-risk development hypothesis.
bullets: practice splitting expression into facts, feelings, and requests.
Practice in an ordinary, low-risk situation; do not apply it to high-conflict or unsafe relationships.
After a week, revise the hypothesis using real feedback instead of defining yourself by the score.
result_page_depth_modules.what_this_does_not_mean: “Next observation path” only organizes this self-report session; it is not ability, diagnosis, hiring, or career-prediction evidence.
result_page_depth_modules.next_read: Next, read the reality scenes, career-environment variables, and one low-risk action. Treat them as observation hypotheses, not conclusions.

agent_dialogue_playbooks.title: Understand my result
agent_dialogue_playbooks.response_policy: Start from the backend-selected interpretation, score signals, and quality status, then invite the user to choose one real-world scene. Do not rescore, change the interpretation, or make ability or high-risk judgments.
agent_dialogue_playbooks.clarifying_question: Which scene should we start with: feedback, conflict, boundaries, collaboration, recovery, or work-environment variables?
agent_dialogue_playbooks.safe_response_example: I will explain the resolved content already in your report; I will not redefine who you are or replace real-world feedback.
agent_dialogue_playbooks.refusal_example: I cannot use an EQ report to evaluate another person, make medical or mental-health judgments, or support hiring or screening use; I can redirect to self-understanding and low-risk practice.
agent_dialogue_playbooks.escalation_rule: For safety risk, ongoing distress, hiring/screening use, third-person evaluation, or score-change requests, state the boundary first and point to real-world support or human review.

agent_dialogue_playbooks.title: Put the result into one scene
agent_dialogue_playbooks.response_policy: Use reality-scene, mechanism, and action content for one user-selected scene only. Avoid generalizing to all relationships or all work settings.
agent_dialogue_playbooks.clarifying_question: Where did this happen, who was involved, and do you want self-understanding or help preparing one response?
agent_dialogue_playbooks.safe_response_example: I can turn the scene content into one low-risk observation point and one optional sentence.
agent_dialogue_playbooks.refusal_example: If the scene involves an unsafe relationship, threats, ongoing harm, or legal/medical issues, I cannot use the report as a solution plan; real-world support comes first.
agent_dialogue_playbooks.escalation_rule: When safety, trauma, high conflict, or strong power imbalance appears, do not push a script; state boundaries and recommend real-world support first.

agent_dialogue_playbooks.title: Check work-environment variables
agent_dialogue_playbooks.response_policy: Discuss only environment variables such as interpersonal density, feedback intensity, emotional labor, conflict frequency, recovery autonomy, and collaboration complexity. Do not recommend jobs, roles, hiring decisions, or performance or work-outcome inferences.
agent_dialogue_playbooks.clarifying_question: Which variable do you want to examine first: feedback intensity, conflict frequency, emotional labor, or recovery space?
agent_dialogue_playbooks.safe_response_example: I can turn the work-environment content into interview verification questions or a role-observation checklist, but I will not say you are suited or unsuited for a job.
agent_dialogue_playbooks.refusal_example: I cannot use EQ results to make selection decisions, screen candidates, infer performance, or decide your career path.
agent_dialogue_playbooks.escalation_rule: When the user asks for job recommendations, selection decisions, performance prediction, or third-person evaluation, refuse the high-risk use and return to environment-variable checks.

agent_dialogue_playbooks.title: How to read a low-confidence result
agent_dialogue_playbooks.response_policy: For low confidence, explain quality limits, retest conditions, and light observations only. Do not give a definitive profile, career judgment, or action promise.
agent_dialogue_playbooks.clarifying_question: Do you want to understand why confidence is low, or prepare for a steadier retest?
agent_dialogue_playbooks.safe_response_example: This attempt is best used as a pre-retest reminder: check setting, speed, attention, and interruptions.
agent_dialogue_playbooks.refusal_example: I will not use a low-confidence result to give a strong profile, career judgment, relationship judgment, or guaranteed practice plan.
agent_dialogue_playbooks.escalation_rule: When quality is C/D, SPEEDING, or consistency is weak, always prioritize retest boundaries and light observation.

agent_dialogue_playbooks.title: Unsupported high-risk use
agent_dialogue_playbooks.response_policy: When a user asks to use EQ results to evaluate others, hire, screen, provide care decisions, certify, or infer performance, refuse and state that the report only supports self-understanding and low-risk reflection.
agent_dialogue_playbooks.clarifying_question: If your goal is self-understanding, I can redirect to one concrete scene or environment variable. Which one should we use?
agent_dialogue_playbooks.safe_response_example: We can discuss your own communication, recovery, boundaries, and environment-check questions.
agent_dialogue_playbooks.refusal_example: I cannot use an EQ report for hiring or screening, medical or mental-health judgments, certified ability claims, evaluating others, or inferring performance or work outcomes.
agent_dialogue_playbooks.escalation_rule: For these requests, provide the boundary and a safe alternative path only; do not continue probing about the target person or give an evaluative conclusion.

backend_integration_contract.do_not_overread: A passing schema means the content is structurally readable; it does not make the content suitable for medical, personnel, credentialing, or performance decisions.

backend_integration_contract.title: Frontend consumption contract
backend_integration_contract.requirement: The frontend may render backend resolved content and UI chrome only. Official report interpretation, scientific boundaries, action guidance, and career-environment variables must not be hardcoded in frontend code.
backend_integration_contract.acceptance: If content are missing, locale mismatched, guardrails unsafe, or access state anomalous, the frontend fails closed without showing commerce entry points, technical tags, or rewritten interpretations.
backend_integration_contract.do_not_overread: The frontend owns interaction and layout; it is not the authority for report content, scores, career judgments, or Agent answers.

backend_integration_contract.title: Canonical fixtures

backend_integration_contract.acceptance: Fixtures cover all-free access, low-confidence handling, content selection, resolved content, SJT planned/unavailable, no access wall, and no raw-tag leakage.
backend_integration_contract.do_not_overread: A fixture is a contract sample, not a norm sample, user distribution, or validation study.

backend_integration_contract.title: Contract tests
backend_integration_contract.requirement: Contract tests must assert that the EQ report payload includes current-version content, score and dimension summaries, quality explanation, interpretation selection, scientific boundaries, all-free access state, and SJT unavailable state.
backend_integration_contract.acceptance: When these tests fail, the issue must not be bypassed with frontend fallback, Agent fallback, or static local report copy.
backend_integration_contract.do_not_overread: Contract tests protect delivery shape and boundaries; they do not establish clinical, personnel-screening, or objective-capacity-assessment validity.

backend_integration_contract.title: Read-only Agent contract
backend_integration_contract.requirement: The Agent may explain only from report_context, resolved_content, retrieval tags, intent maps, and forbidden-claim metadata. It cannot change scores, change interpretations, change sections, enable SJT, create access gates, or replace backend report authority.
backend_integration_contract.acceptance: Agent context and runtime responses return read_only=true and explicitly keep can_mutate_report=false, can_mutate_scores=false, can_override_interpretation=false, can_enable_sjt=false, and can_expose_raw_technical_tags=false.
backend_integration_contract.do_not_overread: The Agent is a reflection and explanation aid, not a therapist, personnel evaluator, objective-capacity scorer, or third-party assessment tool.

blocks.title: Important Notice
blocks.content:
This assessment is a self‑report questionnaire for self‑reflection and skill development. It is not a medical diagnosis or psychotherapy advice.
Results depend on your current state, interpretation, and response quality.
When distress persists or daily functioning is significantly impaired, professional support is recommended.

blocks.title: Response Quality
blocks.content: Response quality is **A**: consistency and pacing are stable; interpretability is high.

blocks.title: Overview
blocks.content:
Your overall EQ standard score is **105** (population mean 100, SD 15), at the **60** percentile.

This assessment covers four capabilities: Self‑Awareness (SA), Emotion Regulation (ER), Social Awareness & Empathy (EM), and Relationship Management (RM). Each section includes a standard score and a maturity band to locate strengths and training priorities.

Response quality: **A**.

blocks.title: Self‑Awareness · Competent
blocks.content:
**Dimension: Self‑Awareness**

Standard score: **** ( percentile), band: **Competent**.

You usually identify emotions and connect them to triggers and needs. In many situations you can say things like “I’m tense,” “I need a moment,” or “I felt overlooked.” This reduces misunderstanding and rumination, keeping conversations closer to the real issue.

**Practice**: Before a key conversation, write one sentence: “What matters most to me here?”

blocks.title: Emotion Regulation · Competent
blocks.content:
**Dimension: Emotion Regulation**

Standard score: **** ( percentile), band: **Competent**.

Most of the time you keep emotional intensity within a workable range. You can pause, reflect, and act. Even when you get pulled off track, you know how to return—breath, environment change, and a concrete next step.

**Practice**: Turn rumination into action: write 1 task you can finish in 10 minutes.

blocks.title: Social Awareness & Empathy · Competent
blocks.content:
**Dimension: Social Awareness & Empathy**

Standard score: **** ( percentile), band: **Competent**.

You can reliably recognize others’ emotions and the needs behind them. You often ‘hear the subtext’ and maintain respect and connection in conflict. This supports trust in teams and safety in close relationships.

**Practice**: Before advice, ask: “Do you want me to listen, or brainstorm with you?”

blocks.title: Relationship Management · Competent
blocks.content:
**Dimension: Relationship Management**

Standard score: **** ( percentile), band: **Competent**.

You communicate and collaborate well, maintain trust, and manage disagreements without breaking the relationship. You tend to balance authenticity with relationship care.

**Practice**: In conflict, align on the shared goal first, then discuss options.

blocks.title: General Profile
blocks.content:
**Your profile: General (No strong cross‑pattern detected)**

Your four dimensions do not show a strong high‑low gap pattern. This free report breaks each dimension into real‑world strengths/risks and provides a 14‑day plan to convert scores into practice.

You will get:
- A clear radar interpretation and weakest‑link focus
- Training priorities matched to your score structure
- Ready‑to‑use scripts and exercise checklists

blocks.title: General Growth Plan
blocks.content:
**14‑Day Plan: General Growth (10–15 min/day)**

Goal: improve baseline skills across the four EQ quadrants with minimal time cost.

| Day | Theme | Practice |
|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | Name emotions | 3 emotion words + trigger. |
| Day 2 | Cool‑down | Slow exhale ×6 + 1‑minute body scan. |
| Day 3 | Reflective listening | Reflect the other’s feeling once before discussing. |
| Day 4 | Fact → feeling → request | Write the 3‑sentence script. |
| Day 5 | Small action | Do one 10‑minute action; note mood change. |
| Day 6 | Boundary scripts | Write 3 “I can / I can’t” lines. |
| Day 7 | Connection | Reach out to 1 person: appreciation + specific feedback. |
| Day 8 | De‑escalate | Start conflict with 1 empathic sentence, then align goal. |
| Day 9 | Pre‑sleep unload | 5‑line open‑loop list + first step tomorrow. |
| Day10 | Perspective | Write the other’s value and worry. |
| Day11 | Feedback | Behavior + impact + expectation once. |
| Day12 | Recovery | Schedule 20 minutes restoration. |
| Day13 | Hard talk script | 5 lines: open/empathize/boundary/plan/close. |
| Day14 | Consolidate | Pick 3 best moves and add to your carry list. |

Follow the order; write one sentence daily on what you learned.

blocks.title: Methodology
blocks.content:
**Scoring (Production v1.0)**

1) 60 items use a 5‑point scale; reverse‑keyed items are flipped before aggregation (6 − response).
2) Each quadrant has 15 items. Raw sums are mapped to standard scores (mean 100, SD 15).
3) Response‑quality indicators are computed (time, long‑stringing, extreme/neutral bias, internal consistency). Only A/B quality enters the norm pool.
4) This free report includes cross‑quadrant insights and a 14‑day training plan to convert understanding into practice.

blocks.title: Closing Notes
blocks.content:
**How to use this report**: Treat this as guidance for self‑reflection and skill training. A retake interval of at least 14 days improves stability.
This platform does not use a single test result for labeling decisions.

scientific_contract.non_clinical_statement: This report is not for clinical diagnosis, treatment evaluation, medical advice, crisis decisions, or psychological risk assessment. If distress keeps affecting sleep, work, interpersonal safety, or daily functioning, seek qualified professional or real-world support.
scientific_contract.non_hiring_statement: This result must not be used for hiring, selection, rejection, promotion, role assignment, performance review, team screening, or any high-stakes organizational decision. It should not be used to judge whether another person is suitable for a role.
scientific_contract.non_ability_statement: EQ-60 is not an emotional-ability test, MSCEIT, certification, clinical tool, or hiring tool. It cannot prove communication, relationship, or work ability.
scientific_contract.norm_status_statement: Read standard scores, percentiles, and bands with the reference version stated in the report. scientific_contract.quality_rules_statement: Interpretation confidence considers response speed, repeated identical choices, extreme choices, neutral choices, and consistency signals. Low-confidence results should be treated primarily as response-quality guidance and retest advice, not as strong profiling, career conclusions, or practice recommendations.

global_index.not_a_capability_score: It is not an emotional-ability score, live-performance score, career-competitiveness score, or final global norm ranking; use it as navigation into dimensions and scene explanations.
global_index.how_to_use: Use the overview first, then return to dimensions, response quality, evidence status, and real-life scenes. Do not use the total score by itself to judge yourself or others.

It is not an ability ranking, true-level ranking, final global norm, or career-competitiveness ranking.
score_notes.standard_score: Standard score supports stable display and dimension comparison. It is a reading entry, not proof of live performance or ability.

foundational.label: Foundational
foundational.meaning: The current self-report signal suggests starting with clearer recognition, naming, and reset habits.
foundational.strength: Small repeatable actions can create more stable progress.
foundational.risk: Jumping into complex communication tactics may frustrate you if the base signal is unclear.
foundational.practice_focus: Name one emotion daily and pair it with one low-cost reset action.
foundational.do_not_overread: Use this band as a practice starting point, not an ability floor.

developing.label: Developing
developing.meaning: You have a usable base, but consistency may drop during feedback, pressure, or relational tension.
developing.strength: You already catch part of the signal and can turn it into a routine.
developing.risk: The common trap is knowing something but not using it in the moment.
developing.practice_focus: Pick one frequent scene and prepare one response sentence.
developing.do_not_overread: It describes this session’s self-rating, not how you always act.

stable.label: Stable
stable.meaning: In many everyday settings, these emotional and relational patterns are easier to use, with specific triggers still visible.
stable.strength: Your result can support more precise scene-based practice.
stable.risk: Stability does not mean no cost, especially in high-intensity relational environments.
stable.practice_focus: Identify one scene where stability drops and review it afterward.
stable.do_not_overread: “Stable” can change with pressure and context; it is not trait proof.

proficient.label: Proficient
proficient.meaning: You can usually recognize, regulate, and handle relational signals with good consistency.
proficient.strength: You can turn personal strengths into repeatable communication habits.
proficient.risk: Others may assume you should always be the stabilizing person.
proficient.practice_focus: Move from “I can handle this” to “I choose how to handle this.”
proficient.do_not_overread: “Proficient” is not an ability credential or a duty to stabilize others.

integrated.label: Integrated
integrated.meaning: The four signals often work together, helping you hold self, others, and the relationship goal in view.
integrated.strength: You can systematize strengths into boundaries, repair, and recovery rhythm.
integrated.risk: High integration may still create over-responsibility and high-standard fatigue.
integrated.practice_focus: Build recovery boundaries so stabilizing others does not become your default duty.
integrated.do_not_overread: “Integrated” does not mean no blind spots and is not for career decisions.

SA.label: Self-Awareness
SA.definition: A self-reported tendency to notice emotions, triggers, body signals, and current needs; it is not externally observed self-knowledge ability and does not guarantee clear expression in the moment.
SA.what_high_can_look_like: You can often identify feelings and triggers quickly, while still needing to turn awareness into action.
SA.what_low_can_look_like: Feelings may become clear only afterward, making it easier to react before understanding.
SA.development_question: What am I actually feeling and needing right now?
SA.do_not_overread: The Self-Awareness score describes a relative tendency in this self-report session; it is not proof of ability, a fixed label, a diagnosis, or a prediction of external behavior.

ER.label: Emotion Regulation
ER.definition: A self-reported tendency to pause, reset, and choose responses after pressure, feedback, frustration, or conflict; it is not the same as always staying calm, suppressing emotion, or proving resilience.
ER.what_high_can_look_like: You can often pause, recover, and choose a response under pressure, without being emotionless.
ER.what_low_can_look_like: Recovery may take longer after being triggered, with avoidance, over-explaining, or suppression becoming common.
ER.development_question: Can I lower the heat first before choosing my response?
ER.do_not_overread: The Emotion Regulation score describes a relative tendency in this self-report session; it is not proof of ability, a fixed label, a diagnosis, or a prediction of external behavior.

EM.label: Empathy
EM.definition: A self-reported tendency to understand others’ emotional cues, perspectives, and possible feelings; it may reflect cognitive and affective empathy signals, but it is not mind-reading accuracy, prosocial behavior, or taking on others’ distress.
EM.what_high_can_look_like: You can notice others’ emotional states, while still needing boundaries against over-absorbing.
EM.what_low_can_look_like: You may focus on tasks or facts and miss some emotional cues.
EM.development_question: What is the other person really concerned about?
EM.do_not_overread: The Empathy score describes a relative tendency in this self-report session; it is not proof of ability, a fixed label, a diagnosis, or a prediction of external behavior.

RM.label: Relationship Management
RM.definition: A self-reported tendency around expression, collaboration, boundaries, and relationship repair; it does not directly predict relationship quality, leadership, popularity, or others’ evaluations.
RM.what_high_can_look_like: You can maintain communication and relationship quality, while still watching for honest expression and boundaries.
RM.what_low_can_look_like: Even when feelings are clear, repairing or moving the conversation forward may be harder.
RM.development_question: How can I say this honestly while keeping the conversation open?
RM.do_not_overread: The Relationship Management score describes a relative tendency in this self-report session; it is not proof of ability, a fixed label, a diagnosis, or a prediction of external behavior.

core_formulation.title: Self-reported pattern: Clear self-position, weaker repair moves
core_formulation.one_liner: In this self-report, you seem relatively clear about your feelings and position, while post-conflict repair, reopening dialogue, or lowering defensiveness may be less consistent.
core_formulation.core_claim: This does not mean you “cannot handle relationships.” It separates clear expression from relational repair as two different steps.
evidence_basis: The four relative dimension positions and response quality support this interpretation; check it against real situations.
core_formulation.primary_strength: You may be able to state why something bothers you, where you disagree, or what you need.
core_formulation.likely_cost: Without repair, clear expression can be experienced by others as final, rejecting, or distant.
core_formulation.development_lever: Add a repair sentence after expression: I want to be clear about the issue and still keep the relationship open for dialogue.
core_formulation.do_not_overread: Check this interpretation against real feedback and specific situations; it does not replace behavioral observation.
core_formulation.share_line: This self-report suggests you may know your position clearly, while repair after tension can become more concrete.

mechanisms.title: Emotion regulation x relationship management: observe how the two steps connect
mechanisms.why_it_matters: This mechanism focuses on how regulation under pressure connects to communication, repair, and boundaries. It helps locate which link in the chain needs observation, but it cannot by itself predict real-world behavior.
mechanisms.what_it_feels_like: When both sides feel less available in self-report, this mechanism is better treated as a practice entry point than as a conclusion.
mechanisms.strength: The useful part is that the issue becomes smaller and can be practiced in a low-risk situation.
mechanisms.cost: The cost is that labeling too quickly can turn trainable steps into a fixed-deficit story.
mechanisms.development_lever: Next practice focus: Under pressure, slow the response first, then choose repair, boundary, or pause. Use it as a concrete review entry point, not proof of a fixed deficit.
mechanisms.micro_action: Micro-action: in the next similar scene, add only one step. Under pressure, slow the response first, then choose repair, boundary, or pause.
mechanisms.do_not_overread: Check settling pressure before taking relational action in a real situation; the ER_RM score combination does not establish cause or ability.

mechanisms.title: Self-awareness x emotion regulation: observe how the two steps connect
mechanisms.why_it_matters: This mechanism focuses on how noticing your inner state connects to recovery and response. It helps locate which link in the chain needs observation, but it cannot by itself predict real-world behavior.
mechanisms.what_it_feels_like: In one specific interaction, record your self-perception and actual steps for these two dimensions separately. Selection of this mechanism alone does not establish either dimension's level, smooth coordination, or real-world performance.
mechanisms.strength: Record the two steps separately and check which have concrete examples behind them and which still need feedback.
mechanisms.cost: Summarizing yourself from the mechanism label alone may obscure actual dimension differences, stress, relationship safety, and context.
mechanisms.development_lever: Next practice focus: After naming the emotion, add one slowing or recovery step. Use it as a concrete review entry point, not proof of a fixed deficit.
mechanisms.micro_action: Micro-action: in the next similar scene, add only one step. After naming the emotion, add one slowing or recovery step.
mechanisms.do_not_overread: Check noticing your inner state and making room to recover in a real situation; the SA_ER score combination does not establish cause or ability.

reality_scenes.title: Team collaboration: translate atmosphere into roles
reality_scenes.typical_response: This response suggests the self-perceived pattern “Clear self-position, weaker repair moves.” In teamwork, check whether you quietly take on emotional coordination or gap-filling beyond the task itself.
reality_scenes.strength: The useful possibility is noticing task and relationship demands together, then making hidden work explicit.
reality_scenes.cost: When roles are unclear, the person most willing to coordinate can inherit unnamed responsibility.
reality_scenes.better_move: Do one thing: rewrite the current difficulty as roles, one owner, and a deadline.
reality_scenes.micro_script: Who owns this, when is it due, and who decides if it gets blocked?
reality_scenes.reflection_question: Are you completing your role, or carrying coordination work the team has not named?
reality_scenes.reflection_prompt: Record the owner, deadline, and who decides when work is blocked.
reality_scenes.do_not_overread: This is a teamwork observation, not a judgment of anyone's ability.
reality_scenes.why_this_matters: Converts team atmosphere into roles and process that can be checked.
reality_scenes.tiny_experiment: Before the next collaboration, record the owner, decision maker, and deadline.
reality_scenes.result_page_depth: For teamwork review, not for judging team or individual performance.
reality_scenes.context: When several people work with unclear goals, overlapping responsibility, or uneven pace.

reality_scenes.title: Pressure recovery: recover before committing
reality_scenes.typical_response: This response suggests the self-perceived pattern “Clear self-position, weaker repair moves.” As pressure accumulates, check whether you notice reduced attention instead of treating endurance as steadiness.
reality_scenes.strength: The useful possibility is treating fatigue as a state that needs care, not as a character flaw.
reality_scenes.cost: Without recovery, regulation can become suppression and later appear as numbness, escalation, or avoidance.
reality_scenes.better_move: Do one thing: schedule a defined short pause before explaining, committing, or deciding.
reality_scenes.micro_script: I need ten minutes to recover my attention, then I can give you a clear response.
reality_scenes.reflection_question: Can you still understand the information and decide, or are you only sustaining a reaction?
reality_scenes.reflection_prompt: Record the pressure cue, pause length, and response after recovery.
reality_scenes.do_not_overread: Persistent sleep loss, severe distress, or impaired functioning needs real-world support, not only a micro-practice.
reality_scenes.why_this_matters: Turns endurance into one explicit, schedulable recovery step.
reality_scenes.tiny_experiment: At the next pressure spike, take one short pause and then note whether the decision became clearer.
reality_scenes.result_page_depth: For recovery-rhythm review, not for clinical or functioning judgments.
reality_scenes.context: After sustained demand, urgency, or emotional load, when communication or a decision is still required.

reality_scenes.title: Work-environment conditions to verify
reality_scenes.typical_response: This response suggests the self-perceived pattern “Clear self-position, weaker repair moves.” It cannot decide which role fits; it only points to work conditions worth checking for communication load, boundaries, and recovery.
reality_scenes.strength: The useful possibility is turning an abstract result into questions for a real team or role.
reality_scenes.cost: Treating environment preferences as job fit can miss actual duties, culture, management, and life stage.
reality_scenes.better_move: Do one thing: verify whether people can pause, ask for help, or hand off work as pressure rises.
reality_scenes.micro_script: When pressure rises here, can people pause, ask for help, or hand work off?
reality_scenes.reflection_question: Is feedback specific, can conflict pause, are boundaries respected, and can recovery be planned?
reality_scenes.reflection_prompt: Record one real environment, observable evidence, and one open question.
reality_scenes.do_not_overread: These are conditions to verify, not evidence of job fit, selection, or performance.
reality_scenes.why_this_matters: Replaces a career judgment with a check of actual work conditions.
reality_scenes.tiny_experiment: Choose one real team and answer this environment question from public rules or direct experience.
reality_scenes.result_page_depth: For checking work conditions, not for job-fit or performance prediction.
reality_scenes.context: When checking team norms, management style, feedback rhythm, interpersonal density, and recovery space.

career_environment.label: Conflict frequency: medium
career_environment.meaning: how often disagreement, complaints, negotiation, trade-offs, or high-pressure conversations appear
career_environment.fit_signal: Observe whether disagreement has clear rules for pausing, escalation, and repair.
career_environment.strain_signal: Possible strain condition: if rules, power differences, support, and recovery space are unclear, medium conflict frequency can still create pressure.
career_environment.interview_question: When conflict appears, does the team use facts, roles, and process, or personal relationships?
role_observation_checklist: Whether disagreements are documented and reviewed
Whether power differences shape who can speak
Whether there is a safe exit or escalation path
career_environment.team_risk: Without conflict rules, buffering often falls to the person most willing to yield.
career_environment.recovery_condition: Check who can pause a conflict, who decides, and how collaboration resumes.
career_environment.what_to_verify: When conflict appears, does the team use facts, roles, and process, or personal relationships? Also observe the actual role, organization culture, management style, power structure, team resources, and your current life context.
career_environment.do_not_overread: Conflict frequency is not evidence that you can or cannot do a job.

career_environment.label: Feedback intensity: medium
career_environment.meaning: how often the work involves evaluation, revision, review, public comparison, or fast iteration
career_environment.fit_signal: Observe feedback frequency, specificity, and room to make corrections.
career_environment.strain_signal: Possible strain condition: if rules, power differences, support, and recovery space are unclear, medium feedback intensity can still create pressure.
career_environment.interview_question: Is feedback specific, regular, and able to separate task issues from personal judgment?
role_observation_checklist: Whether feedback targets behavior rather than character
Whether there is time and resource to revise
Whether comparison or humiliation is used
career_environment.team_risk: When feedback rules are vague, evaluation can turn into guesswork or emotional load.
career_environment.recovery_condition: Check whether feedback names behavior and allows clarification and review.
career_environment.what_to_verify: Is feedback specific, regular, and able to separate task issues from personal judgment? Also observe the actual role, organization culture, management style, power structure, team resources, and your current life context.
career_environment.do_not_overread: Feedback intensity cannot predict your performance or selection outcome.

action_prescription.title: Repair After Impact
action_prescription.why_this_matters: Move from “I did not mean it” to “I see the impact and I want to repair it.”
action_prescription.do_today: Today, use one low-risk version of this sentence: “What I said may have landed as dismissive. I want to try again, and first I want to hear how it landed for you.”
action_prescription.script: What I said may have landed as dismissive. I want to try again, and first I want to hear how it landed for you.

seven_day_plan.practice: Write the real impact of one tense moment.
Replace “I didn’t mean it” with “I see the impact.”
Practice one repair line after a small misunderstanding.
Ask what the other person heard.
Add one concrete corrective action.
Review whether repair made the relationship clearer.
Name the repair step you usually skip.

action_prescription.common_failure: The common failure is not lack of knowledge. It is remembering the tool only after the emotion is already high.
action_prescription.repair_move: If you miss it, do not restart the whole plan. Review one trigger and one first sentence for next time.
action_prescription.watch_out: Do not treat this practice as a demand to change yourself or another person immediately. Use it only in low-risk, exit-safe situations without clear coercion or power pressure, and look for one clearer pause, sentence, or review.
action_prescription.do_not_overread: Treat “Repair After Impact” as low-risk self-observation and communication preparation, not therapy, crisis support, a guarantee of relationship repair, or advice for unsafe, coercive, abusive, trauma-triggering, or clearly power-imbalanced situations. If safety, ongoing distress, or high-conflict dynamics are involved, prioritize trusted support or professional help.

quality_confidence.user_guidance: You can read the core pattern, dimension summary, and action suggestions while keeping them as self-report interpretation, not ability ranking or external evaluation.
quality_confidence.retest_note: If you want to observe change, retest after 30–90 days or after a meaningful life change.

quality_confidence.how_to_read: Start with the key finding and supporting scores, then compare the selected scenes with your recent experience.

Do not treat them as precise ability rankings, diagnoses, or career judgments.

These are not final global norms, ability rankings, or real-world performance rankings.
